subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class core browser-plugin config for per-agent/subagent browser profile binding plus per-profile proxy settings, and what security model should gate browser proxy egress and credentials?
rationale: The missing capability is clear from source, but adding it changes public config, browser egress, proxy secrets, and agent/session ownership semantics, which need maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Stage ownership first
options.body: Approve agent/subagent browser profile binding and ownership diagnostics first, while routing proxy transport details through the broader proxy/security design.

options.title: Approve combined browser contract
options.body: Implement per-profile proxy and per-agent defaults together only after specifying SecretRef handling, SSRF fail-closed behavior, status redaction, and resource limits.

options.title: Defer to external orchestration
options.body: Document Remote CDP, Browserless/Browserbase, browser-lock-style wrappers, or ClawHub plugins as the supported path and close only after maintainers reject core config.

recommendation.title: Stage ownership first
recommendation.body: Approve agent/subagent browser profile binding and ownership diagnostics first, while routing proxy transport details through the broader proxy/security design.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent browser profile, browser-plugin ownership, and CDP/security-boundary work make this the strongest routing candidate for the product/security call.
